scenes.text: For forty years, the only witness in the Bellweather case was a hallway clock.
scenes.art_prompt: an old wall clock in a dim hallway of a 1970s house, faded photograph tone

scenes.text: It stopped at 2:13. The suspect swore he was home by two.
scenes.art_prompt: a stopped clock face close up, hands frozen, dust, sepia archival look

scenes.text: Detectives built the whole timeline on those thirteen minutes.
scenes.art_prompt: case notes and photographs spread on a desk, old lamp, sepia tones

scenes.text: Last year, a restorer opened the clock to repair it and found the truth inside.
scenes.art_prompt: hands opening the back of an antique clock with small tools, dust, sepia

scenes.text:
Someone had bent the minute hand by hand. The clock never stopped on its own.
It was stopped for him, by the one person who needed those thirteen minutes.
scenes.art_prompt: a bent clock hand held under a magnifier, sepia archive light, tense

scenes.text: Follow Unsolved Archive for the next file.
scenes.art_prompt: an empty hallway with a single clock on the wall, sepia light, quiet and final
